Hi Asha —

Congrats again on signing — excited to get SolarisAI live. Attached is a working draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a proposed 5-week sprint map that bundles rollout, canary, migration, and training windows. Highlights:

- Week 0: Pre-cutover prep (config, creds, data sync tests)
- Week 1: Canary launch (10% traffic, automated smoke tests)
- Week 2: Ramp & training wave 1 (ops + SRE enablement)
- Week 3: Migration of remaining workloads (staged by region)
- Week 4: Stabilization & handback to your ops team

I added a canary checklist and a training cadence CSV in the attachments. Can you confirm procurement has visibility to the timeline? Also need to lock in a kickoff date — our team is available the week of Jul 31 or Aug 7.

If it helps, Marissa will lead the onboarding program and Ben will own canary orchestration.

Next steps suggested:
1) Review MAP and mark any gating items in column "Customer asks"
2) Procurement confirms PO and signature acceptance criteria
3) Agree kickoff date and the first training session

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally to assign engineers to the pre-cutover tests.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Dylan / Marissa —

Quick technical notes on the canary request:

- 72-hour canary: feasible for traffic shaping; our engine supports health checks at 15m intervals and automated rollback triggers.
- Two caveats: (1) If the model variant uses KV cache pre-warming across GPUs, the first 6–12 hours will show warm-up variability — we'll need to ignore the initial 15m window metrics for rollback calculus. (2) If traffic is multi-region, we should stage the canary by region to avoid correlated rollbacks.

Proposed compromise: implement a 72-hour canary with an initial warm-up waiver (first 12 hours excluded from rollback triggers) and hourly latency percentiles reported to the MAP dashboard. I attached a short canary-checklist pdf with runbook steps.

I'll also prepare a short smoke-test script for the pre-cutover data sync (to be executed by the SolarisAI SREs).

Ben

Redwood Inference
